clue.text: Film star looks back across time

indicators.note: across says the reversed word lies over the time letter, holding it inside
back says the word for looks is read from right to left

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, so looks gives peers

explanation.surface: A cinema idol gazes back over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEERS into SREEP, and 'across' puts T inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl of that surname is a multi-Oscar-winning Hollywood actress, so she is a film star.

clue.text: Workers dressing very Gallic femme fatale

indicators.note: dressing means clothing, so the workers word wraps round the French word

parts.note: temps are temporary workers
très is French for very

explanation.surface: Office staff dress up a seductive woman in very French style.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductress who lures men to their ruin is the classic femme fatale.

clue.text: Bug, one way or another

parts.note: bug as a noun is an insect, and as a verb means to eavesdrop; the answer is both

explanation.surface: An insect, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an insect with pincers, and as a verb it means to listen in secretly, like a hidden microphone.

clue.text: Long job for Spinoza, say

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
a job in criminal slang is a robbery, a heist

explanation.surface: A lengthy task suited to the Dutch philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long job' reads as a lengthy task; 'Long' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinoza identified God with nature, the defining belief of this school, so he is an example.

clue.text: A European, in essence, is a discriminating sort

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the European letter within the word for essence

parts.note: the gist of something is its essence

explanation.surface: A European at heart is said to be a person of refined discernment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discriminating' reads as discerning, but here it means prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced against people because of how old they are discriminates, which makes them this sort.

clue.text: Foreign film concerning extremely delectable baked dish

parts.note: about means concerning

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of delectable

parts.note: a soufflé is a light baked egg dish

explanation.surface: A foreign film about an exquisite oven-baked dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Godard's 1960 New Wave classic, known in English as Breathless, is a French film.

clue.text: Criminal sent a group of spies in Escobar's ranch?

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters of sent a are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A crook sends a spy ring to a drug lord's ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pablo Escobar was a Colombian drug lord, so his ranch would carry the Spanish-American name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Spanish-American word for a large cattle ranch, fitting a Latin American owner.

clue.text: Audibly breathe hard, racing in cars like RoboCop?

indicators.note: audibly means the word for breathing hard is taken as it is heard

parts.note: to sigh is to breathe out heavily
Formula One, F1, is top car racing, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Panting loudly while racing about in cars, like a cyborg policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: RoboCop is a 1987 film about a cyborg police officer, a classic of the speculative fiction genre.

clue.text: Big hit from poet one translated

parts.note: Homer was the Greek epic poet of the Iliad
un is one put into French

explanation.surface: A poet's work translated becomes a huge success.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the biggest hit sends the ball out of the park, letting the batter circle all the bases.

clue.text: Official on course to give one power to stop escapade

parts.note: to hand is to give
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the power letter plugs the escapade word, stopping it up

parts.note: a caper is an escapade

explanation.surface: A racecourse official grants someone the power to halt a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' reads as prevent; here it means plug.
explanation.definitionFit: At a racecourse, this official assigns weights to horses to even out the race.

clue.text: East of Berlin, privileged person denying reality

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east, the east as Berlin would say it
the rich are the privileged

explanation.surface: Somewhere east of Berlin a well-off person refuses to face facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East of Berlin' looks like a place, but it means the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: The big bird supposedly buries its head in the sand, so the name is used for anyone who ignores unwelcome truths.

clue.text: Battling hard with English soldiers

indicators.note: battling means struggling, so the letters of hard and English are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers fighting fiercely alongside the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Highland regiments of the British Army are made up of Scottish soldiers bearing this name.

clue.text: No fool, Henry has status still

parts.note: taken as written
a twit is a fool
H is the abbreviation for henry, the SI unit of inductance
standing means status or rank

explanation.surface: Henry is no fool and still enjoys high status.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nevertheless or all the same, as in 'still, I went'.

clue.text: President with a place to get a Cabinet?

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower
taken as written

explanation.surface: A president goes somewhere to choose his government ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes Cabinet look like a body of ministers; it is just furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish flat-pack furniture store sells cupboards, so it is a place to buy one.

clue.text: Superior papers rejected by lad, if Sun's out

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters for papers are read backwards

parts.note: ID papers are identity documents

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of lad, if and Sun are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man spurns the newspapers if the Sun is not published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ID into DI; 'out' rearranges LADIFSUN to SDAINFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior as an adjective means haughty or looking down on others, which is scornful.

clue.text: See 5
Pay John's tab for free

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
john is US slang for a toilet, so johns are loos
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone pays John's bill so he goes free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John's' looks like a possessive; it is a plural, johns.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fancy-free and unattached means being at liberty to go anywhere.

clue.text: Film director penning bit of work — it provokes a reaction

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the director's name holds the unit of work

parts.note: Woody Allen is a film director
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A director writes a piece that gets a strong response from audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as pollen that triggers an immune response in the body is called this.

clue.text: A distraught sob by musician who dislikes Fifty Shades of Grey?

definitions.text: who dislikes Fifty Shades of Grey?
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a person, one who dislikes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: distraught means upset and disordered, so the letters of sob are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
a lutist plays the lute

explanation.surface: A tearful musician sobs, disapproving of the racy bestseller.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel's title is read literally: someone who sees only black and white would dislike fifty shades of grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds principles as absolute sees no middle ground, so has no time for shades of grey.

clue.text: Cry to encourage idiot

definitions.meaning: a shout urging someone to continue

explanation.surface: Shouting encouragement at a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is the cheer; as one it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is the urging shout; joined it is slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Group send rude messages on film

parts.note: to sext is to send sexual text messages
ET is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A group sends lewd texts about a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of six performers or things forms a group, especially in music.

clue.text: Doorman to put up with dirty work based in Cambridge

parts.note: a porter guards a door, as at a college or hotel
to house someone is to put them up
blue means risqué or smutty

explanation.surface: A doorman must tolerate grubby chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like tolerate; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sharpe's comic novel is set in a fictional Cambridge college, so it is a literary work based there.

clue.text: Republican, say, is one in party

parts.note: to aver is to say firmly

explanation.surface: A Republican is reportedly a member of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics; it means a wild celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to lively all-night dance gatherings is a partygoer of this kind.

clue.text: Took case of euphoriants in place of spirits

parts.note: had means took, as in had a drink

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone took a box of drugs into a ghostly place.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the underworld is where the shades of the dead dwell.

clue.text: Awful-looking artist getting very old

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
aged means old

explanation.surface: A painter looks terrible as he grows very old.
explanation.definitionFit: A face ravaged by time or illness is badly damaged and looks awful.

clue.text: Well-fed earl leaves lodgings and works out

parts.note: fat means well-fed

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the earl letter goes out of the lodgings word

parts.note: homes are lodgings

explanation.surface: A portly earl moves out and goes to the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works out' suggests exercise; it means figures out.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of something is to figure out or understand it, in the sense of solving it.

clue.text: Councillor with responsibility for 22's old man

parts.note: an onus is a responsibility or burden

explanation.surface: A councillor holds responsibility for a neighbour's elderly husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' is slang for father; 22 is the god of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Titan fathered the ruler of the underworld, the answer at 22-down.

clue.text: Dish carried by salver, as the English say

indicators.note: says the phrase for carried on a salver is spoken in an English accent to give the answer

parts.note: a salver is a tray, so something carried by it is on a tray

explanation.surface: A dish is brought on a silver platter, as the English put it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic English accent, 'on tray' is said the same as the French-derived dish name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a course of a meal, a main dish in the US or a starter in Britain.
